title: North Korea Tests Upgraded 240mm Guided Multiple Rocket Launcher Aimed at Southern Border
detail: North Korea test-fired an upgraded 240mm guided multiple rocket launcher system on September 22, 2026, KCNA reported two days later on September 24. The range-extended rockets use an autonomous precision-guidance system and can strike targets 100 km away in a standard trajectory and 115 km away in a combined glide mode, a precision improvement analysts say could let North Korea hit targets in the Seoul metropolitan area within a few meters of error. Pak Jong-chon, vice-chairman of the Workers' Party Central Military Commission, oversaw the test and said it 'assures' a 'significant change' in firepower readiness along the inter-Korean border, stressing the need to concentrate the 'deadliest and most destructive attack forces' there. KCNA said the test was conducted under North Korea's five-year plan for modernizing its artillery and missile forces.

title: North Korea Sends Vice Foreign Minister Kim Son-gyong to UN General Assembly — First Minister-Level Attendance Since 2019
detail: A DPRK delegation led by Vice Foreign Minister Kim Son-gyong departed Pyongyang on September 22, 2026 to attend the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York, KCNA confirmed. It marks North Korea's first minister-level attendance at the UNGA in six years, since the diplomatic freeze that followed the failed February 2019 Hanoi summit between Kim Jong-un and President Trump. Kim Son-gyong is scheduled to address the General Assembly on September 28 and is expected to meet UN Secretary-General António Guterres as well as officials from allied states including Cuba and Venezuela. Yonhap had first reported the planned attendance on September 17; South Korean officials expect Kim to reiterate Pyongyang's position that it will never abandon its nuclear arsenal, consistent with Foreign Minister Choe Son-hui's September 24 'forever' statement.
